name: Thomas Jefferson
description: US president associated with religious liberty, agrarian republicanism, the Louisiana Purchase and the trade embargo.

axes.brief: Elections, representative republicanism and opposition to sedition laws supported accountability.
axes.counter: Universal adult suffrage was outside his institutions; slavery and unequal citizenship persisted.

axes.brief: A limited government and repeal of coercive federal measures favoured civil liberty.
axes.counter: Embargo enforcement and slaveholding were major contradictions in practice.

axes.brief: Common civic allegiance and Indigenous assimilation supplied national integration context.
axes.counter: Religious pluralism was protected; racial hierarchy qualified universal cultural inclusion.

axes.brief: Reduced naturalisation residency requirements supported immigrant settlement.
axes.counter: Naturalisation remained racially restricted and did not imply today’s universal refugee or welfare rights.

axes.brief: Reduced standing forces and neutrality favoured limiting war.
axes.counter: The Barbary conflict and military embargo enforcement were concrete uses of force.

axes.brief: National independence and avoidance of European entanglements constrained foreign commitments.
axes.counter: Commerce and diplomacy still served national prosperity.

axes.brief: Independent private agriculture and frugal public administration were preferred.
axes.counter: Public postal, military and educational functions qualified universal private provision.

axes.brief: The broad embargo restricted trade to avoid war and defend neutral commerce.
axes.counter: This emergency measure contradicted his usual preference for freer exchange.

axes.brief: Ordinary private production was favoured with reduced federal expenditure.
axes.counter: The embargo directed commerce and relied on coercive enforcement.

axes.brief: Debt reduction and lower internal taxes prioritised property retention.
axes.counter: Broad distribution of opportunity and access to land differed from modern cash equalisation.

axes.brief: Separation of church and state and freedom of religious conscience were explicit commitments.
axes.counter: Cultural religious holidays did not amount to religious legal authority.

axes.brief: Conventional gender roles and sexual morality accompanied political republicanism.
axes.counter: Political liberty and anti-establishment religion did not entail modern family equality.

axes.brief: Science, exploration and agricultural invention were encouraged.
axes.counter: Modern enhancement safety claims have no direct counterpart in his record.

axes.brief: State authority and decentralised agrarian life were normally favoured.
axes.counter: The Louisiana Purchase and embargo expanded federal action beyond that preference.

axes.brief: His racial comparisons invoked natural differences alongside uncertainty and the effects of slavery.
axes.counter: The record contains tentative, prejudiced conjectures rather than modern scientific evidence; each domain remains an inferred personal estimate.

sources.title: Thomas Jefferson — biography, writings and public-policy record
